questions.title: iPod Interactive Interface
questions.scenario: You are developing an interactive iPod media player interface for a music streaming application. The project is partially complete, and you must implement the remaining structure, styling, and action click logic.
objectives: HTML: In the control buttons area (#controls), add a 'Next' button with id='btn-next' and class='control-btn'. The text inside must be 'Next'.
CSS: In style.css, update the iPod body (.ipod-body) background color to 'pink' (or #ff69b4).

JavaScript: Ensure that clicking each button displays its corresponding action text on the screen (#display-text): Previous -> 'Previous Track', Play -> 'Playing Track', Pause -> 'Paused', Next -> 'Next Track'.
constraints: Do not modify or remove any existing id or class attributes as they are used by automated evaluation scripts.
Ensure the action text matches exactly (case-sensitive and proper spacing).
Preserve existing styles while applying the requested color change.

starterCode.html:
Accenture Music 100%
♫
Ready

solution.explanation:
### Explanation
1. **HTML:** Add `<button id="btn-next" class="control-btn">Next</button>` inside `#controls`.
2. **CSS:** In `.ipod-body`, change `background-color` to `pink` or `#ff69b4`.
3. **JS:** Wire up click event listeners using `document.getElementById` and set `displayText.textContent` for Play, Pause, and Next.
solution.html:
Accenture Music 100%
♫
Ready

questions.title: Interactive Product Rating
questions.scenario: Enhance an interactive product rating interface by enabling users to rate products with star icons. The basic structure is present, but three key functionalities must be implemented.
objectives: HTML: Add five star icons with class 'star' inside the #rating-stars container using Font Awesome 'fa fa-star star' or star symbol.
CSS: Style the .filled class with a color of #ffd700 (gold).
JavaScript: Implement the setRating(rating) function so that clicking any star fills all stars up to that rating with .filled and updates the #rating-value text to 'Rating: X / 5'.
constraints: Do not modify any existing class names or IDs.
Rating display must update immediately when stars are clicked.
Unselected stars must have the .filled class removed.

starterCode.html:
Noise-Cancelling Headphones

Rate this product based on your experience:

Rating: 0 / 5

solution.explanation: ### Explanation 1. **HTML:** Insert 5 star elements inside `#rating-stars` (e.g. `★` or empty ``). 2. **CSS:** Add `.filled { color: #ffd700; }`. 3. **JS:** Loop with `stars.forEach((star, index) => { if (index < rating) star.classList.add('filled'); else star.classList.remove('filled'); });` and update `ratingDisplay.textContent = 'Rating: ' + rating + ' / 5';`.

Rate this product based on your experience:

★ ★ ★ ★ ★

questions.title: Product Search Filter
questions.scenario: You are developing a search filter for an e-commerce website where users can filter a list of fruits or vegetables dynamically in real-time based on their search input.
objectives: HTML: Inside <ul class="product">, add 5 list items (<li>) with a data-name attribute containing their lowercase search tag (e.g., data-name="banana"). Make sure at least one contains 'nana'.
CSS: Set the font size of the list items inside .product to 25px.
JavaScript: Set initial search value to 'nana', implement filterProducts() to toggle item.style.display between '' and 'none' based on str.includes(), run it on load, and listen to the 'input' event.
constraints: Search matching must be case-insensitive.
Clearing the search box must restore visibility to all items.
Do not modify the input ID #search-input or list class .product.

solution.explanation:
### Explanation
1. **HTML:** Add 5 `<li>` tags with `data-name="banana"`, `data-name="orange"`, `data-name="pineapple"`, etc.
2. **CSS:** In `.product li`, add `font-size: 25px;`.
3. **JS:** Set `searchInput.value = 'nana';`, filter in `filterProducts()` checking `item.getAttribute('data-name').toLowerCase().includes(filterValue)`, and attach `searchInput.addEventListener('input', filterProducts);`.
solution.html:
• Banana
  • Orange
  • Pineapple
  • Pomegranate
  • Mango

JavaScript: Implement addToCart(itemName) to find the row matching data-item=itemName, parse current quantity with parseInt(), and increment it by 1.

questions.title: Interactive Carousel / Slider
questions.scenario: You are developing an interactive image carousel / slider component for a web gallery. The basic slides are created, and you must finalize navigation controls, indicators, and circular looping logic.
objectives: HTML: Inside #carousel-indicators, add 3 indicator button elements with class 'indicator' and data-index values 0, 1, and 2.
CSS: Style .slide.active with display: block and opacity: 1, and .indicator.active with background-color: #2563eb.
JavaScript: Implement showSlide(index) to wrap index circularly ((index + total) % total), toggle the 'active' class on slides and indicators, and wire up Prev and Next buttons.

solution.explanation:
### Explanation
1. **HTML:** Add 3 indicator buttons `<button class="indicator active" data-index="0"></button>`, `<button class="indicator" data-index="1"></button>`, `<button class="indicator" data-index="2"></button>`.

questions.title: String Consecutive Character Compression
questions.scenario: Given a randomized string input (e.g. aaaaabcccccd), write a function that replaces all consecutively repeating characters with a single hash (#), while leaving isolated, non-repeating characters untouched. Expected output for aaaaabcccccd is #b#d.
objectives: Iterate through the string identifying runs of identical adjacent characters of length >= 2.
Replace each run of consecutively identical characters with a single '#'.
Preserve single isolated characters as they are.
constraints: String length: 1 to 10^5.
Character set: lowercase English letters.

starterCode.html:
String Consecutive Character Compression

Input: aaaaabcccccd

Expected: #b#d

solution.explanation:
### Explanation
Use a single pass loop. If `str[i] == str[i+1]`, advance until characters differ and append `'#'`. If isolated, append `str[i]`.

String Consecutive Character Compression

Input: aaaaabcccccd

Expected: #b#d

questions.title: Player Sports Registration Query
questions.scenario: Fetch first name, last name, and total number of registered sports for each player who has registered for at least 3 sports.
objectives: JOIN the player table with sports_registration table on player_id.
COUNT number of sport_id per player.
Filter using HAVING count >= 3.
constraints: Aliases must match: First Name, Last Name, Number of Sports Registered.
Filter only Paid registrations.

starterCode.html:
SQL Query Formulation

Write standard SQL query below in the JavaScript string variable.
starterCode.css: pre { background:#0f172a; color:#38bdf8; padding:15px; border-radius:8px; font-size:14px; }

solution.explanation:
### Explanation
```sql
SELECT p.first_name AS "First Name", p.last_name AS "Last Name", COUNT(r.sport_id) AS "Number of Sports Registered"
FROM player p
JOIN registration r ON p.player_id = r.player_id
WHERE r.payment_status = 'Paid'
GROUP BY p.player_id, p.first_name, p.last_name
HAVING COUNT(r.sport_id) >= 3;
```
